text:
emily: heads up — noticed a reproducible spike in ConnectionResetError during our load test when using the python SDK async client with keepalive disabled. starts around ~200 concurrent coroutines. stack shows socket closed in connector.

sam: can you paste the minimal repro and config you used? which SDK version?

emily: SDK v0.9.8. repro snippet below:

emily: ```py
async def hammer():
    async with AsyncClient(max_connections=250, keepalive=False) as c:
        await gather(*(c.generate(prompt) for _ in range(1000)))
```

emily: logs: `ConnectionResetError: [Errno 104] Connection reset by peer` repeated, then a cascade of `RuntimeError: cannot acquire semaphore` in our internal connpool.

raj: hmm that RuntimeError smells like our semaphore counter not being released on low-level transport errors. we added an early-return in the close path in 0.9.7 for perf — maybe regressed.

olivia: saw similar pattern in staging around 03:12 UTC yesterday on the dedicated fleet; memory spike then dropped. didn't capture the exact trace but stack traces looked like semaphore.then -> _release_race.

sam: I can try to reproduce locally. emily — can you run with `PYTHONASYNCIODEBUG=1` and `aiodns` disabled? Also what's your OS?

emily: macos dev machine. repros on linux k8s too. I attached a small trace dump below (stdout):

emily: ```
Exception: ConnectionResetError: [Errno 104]
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/our_sdk/connpool.py", line 312, in _acquire
    await self._semaphore.acquire()
RuntimeError: cannot acquire semaphore
```

ci-bot: test failure: test_connpool_timeout_race (tests/test_connpool.py::TestConnPool) — run #4821

raj: okay I'm 90% sure it's the new fast-close path skipping a finally that releases the semaphore when transport aborts. quick fix is to move release into a ``finally`` block or use `asyncio.shield` around release.

sam: opened a local branch, ran unit tests + a stress script. quick patch looks promising: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/3942 (WIP) — adds a try/finally to guarantee release and a small backoff to avoid tight loops.

emily: tested the patch on the k8s staging job with 500 concurrent coroutines and couldn't reproduce the reset or semaphore errors after ~10m. :tada:

olivia: can we add a small e2e stress job to our release pipeline gating for connpool regressions? maybe a tiny chaos test that toggles keepalive and simulates slow closes.

sam: +1 — I'll add a flaky-stress gate and a targeted unit that simulates transport aborts. also will add a changelog note mentioning session lifecycle change.

raj: filing follow-up to audit other fast paths (timeouts, cancel). also adding more asserts in the connpool to catch negative counters earlier.

emily: thanks team. leaving the staging run on for 30 more minutes, will post results. if green I'll merge the PR and cut a patch release (0.9.9).

ci-bot: staging job 7812: all checks passed.

emily: merged and released 0.9.9-patch. breaking change? no, behavior is a bug fix but callouts in release notes about more robust shutdown semantics.

sam: will follow up with a small docs blurb on recommended keepalive settings for high-concurrency services.

emily: closing the thread once smoke in prod looks ok. thanks!
